open_dispute.definition: A dispute is OPEN when DISPUTE_TRANSITIONS still permits it to move, CLOSED when its transition list is empty, and UNKNOWN otherwise.
open_dispute.why_this_one: It was not a judgement call. DISPUTE_TRANSITIONS (script.js:14897) is the machine resolveDispute actually enforces; the other three readings were opinions. docs_requested is plainly open — the landlord has asked for documents and nobody has decided anything.
open_dispute.derived_not_restated: classify() reads the transition list rather than naming statuses, so a state added to the machine is classified correctly the day it is added. Asserted by adding a state at runtime (A2z/A2y/A2x) and by proving the consumers defer rather than merely agree (B2f-i).
open_dispute.legacy_alias: resolved — not in the machine, but written in stored fixture data and already treated as terminal by command-center.js:84 and ai-workspace.js:405. Evidenced, not assumed.
open_dispute.deliberately_unknown: escalated and withdrawn appear exactly once in the codebase, inside script.js's VALID_DISPUTE_STATUSES, and nothing writes either. Classifying them would be guessing at vocabulary that was proposed and never used.
open_dispute.third_answer_carried: tally() returns open, closed AND unknown with the unrecognised statuses named. total === open + closed + unknown always. Folding unknowns into closed understates what needs attention; folding them into open invents work.

leased_area.definition: Sum of leased_sqft over EVERY tenant, and only when every tenant has one. No filter, no fallback, no substitution.
leased_area.why_the_three_old_rules_are_all_wrong: Each substitutes something for a tenant whose area is unknown: `|| 0` treats it as occupying nothing; `|| sqft` swaps in a different quantity mid-sum (demised area vs the tenant row's own figure); an 'active' filter answers a question no other consumer asks.

occupancy.definition: leasedSqft / totalSqft, from the SAME numerator, so the pair can never contradict each other and are null together.
occupancy.clamp_removed: Math.min(100, ...) is gone from this path. leased > total returns null with reason 'exceeds_total'. That configuration is a contradiction in the stored record — double-counted tenants, a stale suite, a total never updated after a subdivision — and the clamp turned exactly that evidence into a confident 'fully occupied'.
occupancy.property_reference_untouched: PropertyReference.occupancyPct is left exactly as it is. It is a browser UI helper; changing it is a UI change. The record simply stops depending on it.

unresolved_ambiguity_reported_not_guesse.item: tenant-normalize.js resolves leased_sqft as `leased_sqft ?? leasedSqft ?? sqft`, upstream of PropertyArea
unresolved_ambiguity_reported_not_guesse.consequence: A tenant whose demised area was never recorded still reaches the record carrying its rentable figure under the leased name. PropertyArea never substitutes, but it cannot see that the substitution already happened.
unresolved_ambiguity_reported_not_guesse.how_it_is_handled: The declared guarantee for identity.leasedSqft is 'convention', not 'enforced', and the note names tenant-normalize.js. Measured and asserted in D10a-c rather than claimed away.
unresolved_ambiguity_reported_not_guesse.why_not_fixed: Changing the tenant normaliser changes what a tenant record IS on every write path in the product. That is not a coherence change.

out_of_scope_finding_reported_not_fixed.what: VALID_DISPUTE_STATUSES is new Set(['open','resolved','escalated','withdrawn']) — a SECOND dispute vocabulary, sharing only 'open' with the state machine. Any status not in that set is rewritten to 'open'.
out_of_scope_finding_reported_not_fixed.measured: docs_requested -> open, accepted -> open, rejected -> open, nonsense -> open. resolved, escalated and withdrawn pass through.
out_of_scope_finding_reported_not_fixed.consequence: Importing a property silently REOPENS every decided dispute on it. An accepted or rejected dispute comes back as open.
out_of_scope_finding_reported_not_fixed.why_not_fixed_in_m7: It is on the import WRITE path, not on any M1-M6 read surface, and the hydrator never calls it. M7 forbids writes and unrelated fixes. Reported here for a separate decision.
out_of_scope_finding_reported_not_fixed.note: This is a data-integrity defect, not a reporting one. It changes stored records.

shim_boundary.justification: It clears the same bar PropertyReference already clears: a pure module looked up by name at CALL time. property-workspace.js and tenant-space.js are browser-first files that must count open disputes the same way every other consumer does; the alternative is a second copy of the predicate in each, which is the duplication M7 exists to remove.
shim_boundary.safety_asserted_not_argued: test-m2 D7a-c and test-m7 A8/A9 assert no DOM, storage, network or other global access, purity of classify(), and that classifying mutates nothing the module holds.
shim_boundary.bug_this_caught: test-m1b I4 failed because DisputeStatus was DECLARED on the allow-list but never PLACED in the shim — CLEAN modules load with no global installed, so the UMD tail found no window. Both browser files were silently taking their fallbacks, and the single shared definition M7 exists to create was not the one running. Fixed by placing it explicitly, alongside PropertyReference, with the reason recorded in the code.
